title: The Intercom Said It Was My Neighbour. She Moved Out Last Week. (Part 1)

scenes.notes: At three oh seven, my intercom buzzed. The voice said it was June, from downstairs.

messages.text: who keeps leaving the lobby door on the latch
Anyone want my plants before the van comes? 🌿
Farewell to June in 3B! Moving van came today 📦

scenes.notes: But June moved out last Tuesday. The building chat said so.
She sounded tired. Nora, it's June. I locked myself out. Can you buzz me in?

Today 3:08 AM
She's gone. I carried her sofa to the van myself.

scenes.notes: I muted the call and opened the chat. Mr. Okafor in Two-A had written: She's gone. I carried her sofa to the van myself.

scenes.notes: Theo in Six-C replied: Maybe she came back for something? Go to sleep, everyone.
So I tested her. June used to feed my cat, and she kept my spare key. I asked the voice what my cat was called.
She said Pickles. Instantly. She was right.

I'm watching the lobby camera.

scenes.notes: Then Priya in Five-A posted. I'm watching the lobby camera. Nobody is at the front door.
The call dropped on its own. Out in the hall, the elevator started climbing. One. Two. Three. It stopped at June's floor.
Then I heard footsteps right under my feet. Inside the empty flat below me.
The intercom buzzed again. This time the screen didn't say Front Entrance. It said Unit Three-B.
Never mind, Nora, said the voice. I found my keys. I'm home now.

messages.text: Van's here! Thanks for everything, Nora 💛
Safe travels!! Text me when you land
Nora, I'm four hundred miles away. Your spare key is still hanging on the hook inside my door.

scenes.notes: Then a text arrived from June's real number. Nora, I'm four hundred miles away. Your spare key is still hanging on the hook inside my door.
